blocking.finding: L6 (also M4, L2) — the boot-time SIGNED_IN replay now wipes refresh-surviving stores on an ordinary page reload
blocking.problem: src/lib/supabase/client.tsx:290-291 clears every account-scoped store whenever `publishedUserIdRef.current !== nextUserId` on a SIGNED_IN event. `publishedUserIdRef` is only set at client.tsx:248, after `Promise.all([getUser(), getSession()])` — a network round-trip. But @supabase/auth-js 2.112.4 emits SIGNED_IN for a valid stored session during boot (GoTrueClient.js:4152, inside `_recoverAndRefresh`), and `initialize()` (GoTrueClient.js:353-370) flushes that queued event to every registered subscriber the moment `initializePromise` settles — before getUser's fetch resolves. Offline probe with the real GoTrueClient and a non-expired stored session printed `EVENT SIGNED_IN user-a 0 ms` before `INITIAL_SESSION`. So on a full reload of a signed-in tab the handler sees null → 'user-a' and runs `clearAccountScopedBrowserState()`. That was already true for recent queries / answer thread / signed-URL cache (pre-existing, not this package's finding), but this branch extends it to three stores whose contract is the opposite: the Caring Contacts draft (plan-draft.ts:3 'held in the browser so that a page refresh does not lose it' — owner Ruling [110], the workspace is sign-in only, so every F5 now destroys the draft), the patient profile (patient-profile-storage.ts:5 'survives navigation … within a tab session'), and the favourites pins/last-opened keys (localStorage, 90-day TTL, now reset every reload for signed-in users). The timing is a race with React's passive-effect registration of `onAuthStateChange` (client.tsx:277), so the loss is intermittent rather than deterministic — worse, not better. The new test cannot see this: its mocked `onAuthStateChange` (tests/patient-profile-storage-account-transitions.dom.test.tsx:35-38) never replays SIGNED_IN at boot, so `mountAuthenticated()` reaches 'authenticated' without ever exercising the null → user branch.
blocking.required_change: In src/lib/supabase/client.tsx, distinguish the boot replay from a real account transition: add a ref (e.g. `initialSessionPublishedRef`) that `initializeSession` sets to true at line 248 (both branches), and in the onAuthStateChange handler run `clearAccountScopedBrowserState()` only when `initialSessionPublishedRef.current && publishedUserIdRef.current !== nextUserId` — the sign-out (413) and expiry (426) paths already null the ref and clear, so a later sign-in as a different user is still covered and no leak path opens. Then add a test in tests/patient-profile-storage-account-transitions.dom.test.tsx whose mocked `onAuthStateChange` replays `('SIGNED_IN', authApi.session)` synchronously on subscribe while `getUser` is still pending (a deferred promise), seeds the plan draft, patient profile and favourites keys before mount, and asserts all three are still present once status is 'authenticated'; keep the existing user-A → user-B case green. If the implementer prefers to leave the pre-existing recent-query/answer-thread clears on the boot path, gate only the new stores — but state that choice in the commit message.
